verification_report.summary: The full supplied proof, including both preliminary collapse results and the Stone–infinite-star theorem, passes verification. The star comparison inequalities are local and stable under decreasing limits; they imply the finite slope budget and countable activity. The finite harmonic smoothing preserves convexity and restores exact derivative balance, while the quantitative error bounds give decreasing approximations on fixed neighbourhoods. The polar-node and terminal-endpoint cases are also valid. The Stone–Euclidean proof correctly constructs a common countable Boolean quotient, descends upper semicontinuity, and produces decreasing smooth convex approximations, including dimension zero. For the Stone–star product, compact standard cores preserve a common countable activity set under limits; compact parameter maxima preserve endpoint traces and junction inequalities; finite-branch truncations and smoothing yield the claimed fixed-product-neighbourhood approximation. All cited CLD statements and their applications were checked against the July 2025 revision, including the topology, smooth structure, product affinage, and generated psh definition. [CLD source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277). No critical errors or mathematical gaps were found.
